messages:
maria: seeing a spike in apiserver watch latency across eu-west clusters, started around 12:45 UTC. kube-controller-manager is logging a bunch of 'failed to list *v1.Pod: etcdserver: request timed out'. :rotating_light:

sam: same here, controllers keep requeuing. Noticed many watch reconnects in the apiserver logs. Metrics: apiserver_watch_events_total dropped, watch_cache_size stable though.

oj as: can you paste the etcd endpoint status? run: `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=$ENDPOINT endpoint status --write-out=table`

maria: pasted below from eu-west1-primary (sanitized):
```
+------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-----------+
|    ENDPOINT      | STATUS  | DB SIZE | IS LEADER | RAFT TERM |
+------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-----------+
| 10.2.1.5:2379    | healthy | 1.2 GB  | false     | 42        |
| 10.2.1.6:2379    | healthy | 1.2 GB  | true      | 42        |
| 10.2.1.7:2379    | healthy | 1.2 GB  | false     | 41        |
+------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-----------+
```


taylor: RAFT TERM mismatch on one follower (41 vs 42) — suggests recent election or follower lag. Any network blips in the control plane subnet?

maria: cloud metrics show a short packet-drop event from the controller VIP at ~12:44 for ~20s, coincides with when apiserver started pile up.

oncall-lx: I just checked kube-apiserver logs; repeated `watch chan closing` followed by `Unable to decode object` stack traces, then `too many watchers` warnings.

sam: controller-manager backlog grew -> many controllers hitting the leader-elected path but failing list/watch against etcd. This will throttle pod lifecycle and GPU provisioning queues (we have pending node claims for dedicated-gpu pools).

ojas: could be the watch cache eviction behaviour interacting with high cardinality objects — we recently rolled an app that creates lots of ephemeral CRs for training jobs. Any correlation with deployments?

maria: yes, batch-training job ramp started at 12:40 — roughly 800 short-lived job CRs created over 3 mins. Noticed controller-manager attempting to sync them and hitting etcd.

taylor: ops plan suggestion: 1) temporarily pause the batch job submitter, 2) increase etcd request-timeout/heartbeat config as emergency mitigation, 3) consider scaling etcd quorum (add a warm follower) or promote follower catch-up. Thoughts?

oncall-lx: pausing job submitter now. :white_check_mark:

sam: cautious about changing etcd timeouts in prod. I prefer adding capacity or letting follower catch up — it's already lagging. Any idea why follower is behind? Disk iops or CPU?

maria: node metrics on 10.2.1.7 show disk latency spikes around the same time (avg read latency > 20ms) and kubelet saw increased CPU steal.

ojas: could be noisy neighbour on the storage node — we recently expanded GPU fleet in that AZ which may have bumped IO. If IO is saturated, follower can't apply entries -> raft term mismatch.

taylor: short-term: keep job submitter paused, cordon any noisy machines in the same rack, and promote a healthy follower if possible. Long-term: add IO-optimized etcd replicas or move etcd to dedicated NVMe nodes for clusters with heavy ephemeral CR churn.

oncall-lx: deploy-bot reports an ongoing canary deploy in infra/gpu-autoscaler at 12:38 — that added extra watch load by creating per-node leases. Rolling back canary?

maria: canary rollback initiated. deploy-bot: `rollback infra/gpu-autoscaler #canary` -> succeeded.

sam: after rollback, watch reconnects are dropping and controller queue depth is decreasing. Controller-manager errors now down to baseline.

ojas: we should also add guardrails on the batch job submitter to rate-limit CR creation and expose backpressure -> this would keep watch churn bounded and reduce unit cost spikes.

taylor: agreed. Create a short RFC for rate-limits + propose moving etcd to dedicated IO nodes for clusters that serve GPU provisioning workloads. Attach cost vs performance tradeoffs (NVMe reserved vs shared).

maria: for incident notes: root cause = ephemeral CR churn + temporary storage IO saturation on an etcd follower -> follower lag -> raft term mismatch -> apiserver watch reconnect storms -> controller-manager requeues -> provisioning queues stall (affecting GPU claims). Remediations: rollback canary, pause submitter, cordon noisy hosts, let follower catch up.

oncall-lx: monitoring follow-ups: add a single alert that correlates etcd follower applied_index_lag > 50k with apiserver watch reconnect rate > 100/min and controller_manager_queue_depth > 500. Also surface GPU provisioning pending_count in the same dashboard.

sam: logging note: make sure we capture `etcdserver: request timed out` sample window in traces to help future RCA.

maria: closing the thread, creating a postmortem draft. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
